newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia rejects Eurobond delay report.
newsitem.headline: Russia rejects Eurobond delay report.

text.p: A senior Finance Ministry official on Friday rejected reports that Russia's forthcoming mark Eurobond could be delayed.
"The news about a postponement of the Eurobond does not correspond to reality," Dmitry Alexeyev, an official in the foreign credits and external debt department, told Reuters.
He said he was speaking on behalf of First Deputy Finance Minister Andrei Vavilov.

Earlier a syndicate manager at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, joint lead manager of the deal, said Russia may not launch its mark Eurobond next week as expected if sentiment in the emerging market sector of the bond market does not improve.
Russian is holding presentations for investors in Zurich on March 11 and Frankfurt on March 12, and Russian officials said on Thursday the bond could be issued on March 13 after the roadshow.
The bond, for up to two billion marks, is expected to have a maturity of seven years.

The market is talking of a spread of 325-340 basis points over Bunds, but the Deutsche Morgan Grenfell syndicate manager said this could be adjusted in line with the current yield of Russia's dollar eurobond.
Russia's debut $1 billion Eurobond, launched last November, was trading at 325-335 points over U.S. Treasuries at 1230 GMT. It hit 350 earlier this week and was launched at 345 points over.
Emerging market debt prices have fallen since February on worries that U.S. interest rates will rise.
